volume_content_scan.description: When a partition/volume start falls inside the first 64 MiB, a lightweight string/UTF-16 scan looks for OS and role indicators plus interesting paths.
volume_content_scan.notes: Heuristic only. Full directory listings require proper filesystem parsers and, for container formats, virtual-to-physical mapping. Encrypted volumes are skipped. Results appear under volume_summaries, os_hint, and volume_role.

formats.name: Raw Disk Image
formats.description: Unstructured byte-for-byte copy of a disk, partition, or single volume. No container header.
formats.identification: No known container magic. May contain MBR (0x55AA at 510), GPT ('EFI PART' at 512), filesystem signatures at offset 0, LVM label at offset 512, or encryption headers.
formats.notes: v2.0 adds direct filesystem detection for single-partition images and LVM-on-raw detection. Sparse only if host FS supports holes.
formats.sparse: Depends on host FS; typically thick.

formats.name: QEMU Copy-On-Write v2/v3
formats.description: Sparse virtual disk format used by QEMU/KVM.
formats.identification: Magic 'QFI\xfb' at offset 0. Virtual size (BE uint64) at offset 24.
formats.notes: Always sparse. Guest content requires cluster mapping. First 64MB contains header and tables.

formats.name: Virtual Hard Disk (VHD)
formats.description: Microsoft Virtual PC / Hyper-V legacy format. Fixed or dynamic.
formats.identification: Dynamic: 'conectix' at start, size at offset 40. Fixed: footer at end.
formats.notes: Dynamic = sparse. Fixed footer may be missed if only reading start of large files.

formats.name: Virtual Hard Disk v2 (VHDX)
formats.identification: Magic 'vhdxfile' at offset 0. Size in metadata region.

formats.name: VirtualBox Disk Image
formats.identification: Magic 0xBEDA107F at offset 0x40. Size at offset 0x170. Type at ~0x4C.

formats.name: VMware Virtual Machine Disk
formats.identification: 'KDMV' sparse header or '# Disk DescriptorFile' text.
formats.notes: Often sparse. Capacity in header or descriptor.

formats.name: ISO 9660 / UDF
formats.notes: Volume size from PVD. Root directory records available for file listing.

encryption_signatures.name: BitLocker (fixed)
encryption_signatures.notes: Volume header also contains metadata block offsets.

encryption_signatures.name: BitLocker To Go
encryption_signatures.magic: BitLocker identifier GUID (3B D6 67 49 29 2E D8 4A 83 99 F6 A3 39 E3 D0 01)
encryption_signatures.notes: Discovery volume may look like FAT/exFAT; scan first 512 bytes for the GUID.

encryption_signatures.name: LUKS
encryption_signatures.notes: Version at offset 6 (BE uint16). LUKS1 has UUID at offset 168; LUKS2 has JSON metadata.

lvm.name: LVM2 Physical Volume
lvm.notes: Can appear on a raw whole-disk image (no partition table) or inside a partition. Label may be in any of the first 4 sectors. Contains PV UUID.

general_notes: v2.0 adds filesystem, encryption (BitLocker Device ID), and LVM detection.
Single-partition raw images are detected by scanning offset 0 for FS/encryption signatures.
When a partition table exists, filesystem signatures are also checked at each partition start (if within the 64 MiB window).
Container formats still require virtual-to-physical mapping for guest content analysis.
BitLocker Device ID is the volume GUID stored in the clear-text header.
Always prefer content signatures over file extensions.
